belief: “Staying in control keeps me from being controlled.”
belief_plain: Staying in control keeps me from being controlled.
intro: Do you feel you have to be the one in charge, or someone else will have power over you? Does giving way feel like losing? The information below is intended to help you take a step toward strength that does not need to dominate, and to find the security that comes from knowing God’s word as found in the Bible.
origins: Many people who hold this belief were once controlled themselves by a harsh parent, an abusive partner, or a rough environment. The lesson they took was never to be the weak one again. The need to stay on top then becomes a way of staying safe.
keeps: Pushing, intimidating, or winning at all costs can work in the moment, and it leaves others afraid, angry, or distant. Every relationship becomes a contest, and I may feel I can never relax. The strongest bonds, built on trust, never get the chance to form.
teaches: Jesus showed another kind of strength. “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them… But it shall not be this way among you.” And “The Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.” We are told to be “not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.” “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.” Real security comes from God, not from dominating others.
key: You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them. But it shall not be this way among you.
also: Not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
self: If I do not take charge, someone else will.
I will never be pushed around again.
errors: Seeing every relationship as either dominating or being dominated.
Treating everyone as a threat because someone once hurt me.
Predicting that any softness will be exploited.
Feeling threatened and concluding I must dominate.
Assuming people who fear me respect me.
Counting the win and not the damage to relationships.
questions: When did I first feel controlled or powerless?
What do I actually fear would happen if I gave way?
Is it true that everyone is trying to control me?
What has dominating cost me in relationships?
Could I be strong and still gentle?
What does Scripture say about true greatness?
What kind of person do I want to be?
truth: I can be strong without dominating. Real security comes from God, not from controlling people. I can give way, listen, and cooperate without being weak, and gentle strength builds respect that lasts.
prayer: Lord, You know what taught me to fear being controlled. Give me security in You, and teach me a strength that serves instead of dominates. Amen.
clinical: For counselors: this belief appears in the cognitive model of what clinicians call antisocial personality disorder (Beck, Davis, & Freeman, Cognitive Therapy of Personality Disorders), where views such as “I have to look out for myself,” “others are weak and exploitable,” and “rules do not apply to me” are central. A history of being controlled or abused often underlies dominance; address the old injury, reframe strength, and rehearse assertive but non-intimidating behavior. Assess for ongoing violence or intimidation in the home. Expect little spontaneous distress about these beliefs; engagement usually begins with the person’s own goals and costs (relationships, legal trouble, loss of trust), so use collaborative questioning rather than confrontation, set clear boundaries, and keep sessions practical. Assess risk of harm to others, abuse or violence in the home, substance use, and suicide risk; consult or refer as indicated (in the U.S., 988 for crisis). This is an individualized educational formulation, not a DSM criterion or a diagnostic test. Similar presentations can arise from trauma, a hard upbringing, substance use, or other conditions, so careful assessment matters.
morning: Each morning ask: “How can I be strong and kind today?”
catch: “If I do not take charge, I will be controlled.”
hw_truths: I can be strong without dominating.
I can let someone else lead sometimes.
experiments: Let someone else choose in a small matter today.
Ask for another person’s opinion and listen without arguing.
Notice when you feel threatened, and name what you fear.
Practice a calm firm statement instead of a forceful one.
Thank someone who gave way to you.
Pray Mark 10:42–43 before a tense situation.
reflect: After listening to one of the four songs, write a sentence about true strength.
newtruth: I can be strong without dominating. God is my security, and gentle strength earns lasting respect.
prayer2: Lord, thank You for being my security. Teach me a strength that serves. Amen.
